segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Jack, I’m thinking of taking the kids to the seaside on a surfing holiday this summer and I wanted to ask your advice - as I know you’re such an expert.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well, I don’t know about that, but yes, I've done a bit of surfing over the years. I’d thoroughly recommend it. I think it’s the kind of holiday all the family can enjoy together. The thing about surfing is that it's great for all ages and all abilities. My youngest started when he was only three!

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Wow! But it’s quite physically demanding, isn't it? I've heard you need to be pretty fit.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes. You’ll certainly learn more quickly and won't tire as easily.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well - that should be OK for us. You've been surfing a few times in Ireland, haven’t you?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes. There's some great surfing there, which people don’t always realise.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: And which locations would you recommend? - there seem to be quite a few.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes, there are loads. Last year we went to County Donegal. There are several great places to surf there. woman: What about in County Clare? I read that's also really good for surfing.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes, it is. I've been there a few times. Most people go to Lahinch. My kids love it there. The waves aren't too challenging and the town is very lively. woman: Are there good hotels there?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes - some very nice ones and there are also a few basic hostels and campsites. It's great if you need lessons as the surf schools are excellent.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes and there’s lots to see in the area - like those well-known cliffs - ... I’ve forgotten the name of them ...

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh don’t worry - I can look them up.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: I've also been surfing in County Mayo, which is less well-known for surfing, but we had a really good time. That was a few years ago when the kids were younger. There’s a good surf school at Carrowniskev beach.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: How do you spell that?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: C-A-double R-O-W-N-l-S-K-E-Y

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: I put the kids into the surf camp they run during the summer for 10-16 year olds.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh right. How long was that for?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Three hours every day for a week. It was perfect - they were so tired out after that.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I can imagine.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: One thing we did while the kids were surfing was to rent some kayaks to have a look around the bay which is nearby. It’s really beautiful.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Oh, I’d love to do that.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Now the only time I went to Ireland it rained practically every day.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Mmm yes - that can be a problem - but you can surf in the rain, you know.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It doesn’t have the same appeal, somehow.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well, the weather’s been fine the last couple of years when I've been there, but actually, it tends to rain more in August than in the spring or autumn. September's my favourite month because the water is warmer then.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: The only problem is that the kids are back to school then.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: I know. But one good thing about Irish summers is that it doesn't get too hot. The average temperature is about 19 degrees and it usually doesn't go above 25 degrees.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That sounds alright. Now what about costs?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Surfing is a pretty cheap holiday really - the only cost is the hire of equipment. You can expect to pay a daily rate of about 30 euros for the hire of a wetsuit and board - but you can save about 40 euros if you hire by the week.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s not too bad.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: No. It’s important to make sure you get good quality wetsuits - you’ll all get too cold if you don’t. And make sure you also get boots. They keep your feet warm and it's easier to surf with them on too.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. Well, thanks very much ...
